title: Daily and Weekly Home Crop Routine

content.overview: A stable home grow is built from repeatable small tasks. Daily checks catch urgent changes; weekly checks provide deeper inspection and maintenance without requiring constant intervention.

vocabulary.definition: A repeatable sequence of observations and tasks.
The reduction of substrate water content between irrigation events.
Planned inspection or service intended to reduce equipment failure.

sections.title: Daily: observe before acting
sections.body: Check plant posture, substrate/water status, environmental readings, leaks/equipment and obvious pest or disease changes before changing settings.

sections.title: Weekly: inspect deeper
sections.body: Review canopy interior, undersides, irrigation uniformity, sensor agreement, filters/cleanliness and grow-log trends.

sections.title: Irrigation follows the root zone
sections.body: Watering frequency should respond to substrate, root establishment, plant demand and environment rather than a fixed daily ritual.

workedExamples: If pots remain much wetter than normal, investigate demand and root-zone conditions before watering by habit.
A weekly comparison of sensors can catch a drifting humidity probe before it drives unnecessary control changes.
commonMistakes: Watering because the clock says so.
Adjusting setpoints every time a reading moves slightly.
Skipping pest scouting when plants look vigorous.
content.practicalApplication: Create a daily five-minute checklist and weekly 20-minute inspection. Mark only exceptions and meaningful trends so the routine remains sustainable.
content.summary: Simple consistent routines reduce emergencies and teach the grower how normal plant and system behavior looks.
